draft.title: Nutrition for performance
card: The body stores carbohydrate as glycogen in muscles and the liver. Glycogen is a main fuel for moderate to hard exercise, and low stores can lead to early tiredness.
Protein supplies amino acids, which the body uses to repair and build muscle after training.
A meal rich in carbohydrate a few hours before training helps fill glycogen stores. In long sessions, carbohydrate taken during exercise can help keep energy up.
Soon after training, carbohydrate refills glycogen and protein supports muscle repair. Eating both in this period helps recovery.
draft.remember: Carbohydrate fuels the work, protein repairs the muscle, and timing helps both do their job.

a.q: Why does an athlete eat protein after a hard strength session?
opts: To supply amino acids for muscle repair
To supply glycogen for the next session
To supply fluid lost through sweat
To supply fuel for the session just finished
a.why: Protein is broken down into amino acids, which the body uses to repair and build muscle. Glycogen comes from carbohydrate, so the glycogen option is the tempting wrong one.
a.clue: Think about what protein is made of and what the body uses it for.

b.q: Priya has a 90 minute netball training session at 6 pm. Which plan best suits her fuel needs?
opts: Carbohydrate meal before, carbohydrate and protein after
Protein meal before, then only water after
No food before, so she uses her glycogen, then protein after
Carbohydrate meal before, then no food until next morning
b.why: A carbohydrate-rich meal beforehand fills glycogen stores, and carbohydrate with protein soon after refills glycogen and supports muscle repair. The plan with no food beforehand is tempting, but low glycogen can cause early tiredness.
b.clue: Check that each plan covers fuel before and recovery after.

a.best: To supply amino acids for muscle repair

b.best: Carbohydrate meal before, carbohydrate and protein after
